title: Stage 2 Technical Structure, Institutional Flow & Momentum Setup

epigraph.quote: It never was my thinking that made the big money for me. It always was my sitting.
epigraph.author: Edwin Lefèvre, Reminiscences of a Stock Operator, 1923

web_blocks.text: Stan Weinstein's stage analysis sorts every stock into four phases around its 30-week simple moving average (SMA, the average of the last 30 weekly closes). Stage 1 is a flat base after a decline. Stage 2 is the advance, with price above a rising 30-week average. Stage 3 is a topping range and Stage 4 a decline below a falling average. Greaves Cotton is in Stage 2 on our ledger (“Stage 2 (Markup)”) and on the TradingView snapshot [108][118]. That is a permission to consider the stock, not a reason to buy it. Chapter 7 judged the business conditional, so the chart has to earn its place by offering a good price.

Three dating facts bound what follows. The levels use the TradingView snapshot of 13 November, after the NSE close, at ₹225.97. The ledger fields (swing low, ATR, volume multiple, distribution days, relative strength) are from the 12 November bar at ₹223.18, one session older [108][118]. TheWrap's Stage 2 dashboard is dated 8 November and does not list Greaves among its 465 Stage 2 names, so there is no independent leadership confirmation [110]. One possible reason, which we could not verify: the 13 November price and the one-week gain of 11.11% imply a 6 November close near ₹203.4, only 0.4% above the 30-week SMA of ₹202.50 (our calculation [118]). The stock was on the Stage 2 line when the dashboard was built.

On the averages the structure is clean. The close is 8.57% above the 10-week EMA (exponential moving average, which weights recent weeks more) at ₹208.14, 10.69% above the 50-day SMA at ₹204.14, 11.59% above the 30-week SMA at ₹202.50 and 20.83% above the 200-day SMA at ₹187.01 [108]. The 50-day average is rising, from ₹203.18 twenty-one days ago on the ledger, and the 200-day was ₹184.68 sixty-three days ago [118]. The 200-day EMA at ₹197.84, the 20-day SMA at ₹200.31, the 4H 50 SMA at ₹201.80 and the pivot midpoint at ₹200.30 stack into a shelf between about ₹198 and ₹208 [108]. That shelf is where a pullback would find buyers if the trend is healthy.

web_blocks.takeaway: The averages and weekly RSI say a sound uptrend. The shortest clocks and the volume rows say the move is ahead of itself and not yet backed by consistent institutional buying. Both readings are true, so the decision is about price, not trend.

web_blocks.text: The 4H RSI of 71.34 against 66.52 daily and 57.38 weekly is the clearest tempo gap. RSI (relative strength index) scales recent gains against losses from 0 to 100, and above 70 usually means stretched. A hot short clock over a mid-range weekly clock usually resolves by cooling, either a pause or a pullback toward the 4H 20 EMA at ₹211.10 and the 10-week EMA at ₹208.14, while the weekly catches up. The options module labels the setup STAGE2_EXTENDED for the same reason [118].

Overhead supply is the next constraint. Supply here means holders who bought higher and may sell to get even. R1 at ₹229.09 is only 1.4% above the close, and the zone from about ₹230 to ₹272 holds the FY22 high of ₹258.9, the FY26 high of ₹244.3 and the FY27 high of ₹271.9 [108][111]. Our monthly price history gives no volume by price, so the zone is inferred, not measured. Clearing ₹271.90 would remove all of it.

Volume gives mixed evidence. On 13 November the stock traded 2.87 million shares, 1.31x the 30-day average of 2.19 million, as the price rose 1.25% after the Q2 result reported on 29 October [108][24]. That is the single expanded day. If the 10-day average of 1.63 million includes it, the nine sessions before averaged about 1.50 million, roughly 0.68x the 30-day average, so much of the 11% weekly rise came on below-average volume (our calculation [118]). The ledger adds a 12 November volume of 0.61x and six distribution days in 25 sessions, meaning down days on heavier volume. One strong day does not turn that into accumulation.

Relative strength compares the stock with the index. Greaves is +9.46% ahead over 63 sessions but −14.93% behind over 28 on the ledger's measure [118]. We read it as a stock that fell back from its ₹271.90 high and is now rebounding; we could not reconcile it exactly with the +8.1% one-month price gain, because the ledger's window is not shown. The market is in an uptrend with narrow breadth: 61% of the Nifty-500 pool is above its 50-day average and 52% above the 200-day, 3 distribution days sit in 25 sessions, and 9 of 11 sectors are above their 50-day [118]. On TheWrap's 8 November sector density, Engineered Goods is 67% Stage 2, Auto OEM 42%, Auto Ancillary 35%, Pumps 25% and Vehicle Finance 17% [110]. Greaves straddles several, so the sector offers support, not leadership.

web_blocks.takeaway: The two sources agree on every structural point and differ only by the one added bar. The volume rows are not comparable, because they use different averaging windows, so we do not net them into a single flow verdict.

web_blocks.text: The snapshot itself labels the posture BUY_AT_CMP_NO_FOMO and the timing gate CLEAR_FOR_CONSIDERATION, because the extension above the 10-week EMA is 8.57% and the rule caps it at 10%, the point where chasing is blocked. The options module calls the same chart STAGE2_EXTENDED [108][118]. These are not contradictory: the gate says the stock is not yet too far from its average. It is also close to the cap, since 10% above ₹208.14 is about ₹229, almost exactly R1 (our calculation [118]). A few percent more and the gate itself would flip. Our posture is WAIT_FOR_SUPPORT on a TIER_3 TACTICAL_MOMENTUM idea.

Does a short-term momentum edge exist now? Our judgment is no, for chasing. The close is 2.23 ATRs above the 50-day, the 4H RSI is above 70, the nearest supply sits 1.4% above, volume has been uneven and the 28-day relative strength is negative. A breakout buyer needs a strong volume break above supply, and we do not have one. The edge is in buying the pullback to ₹205.02-₹211.26 with a ₹197.60 stop. Asymmetry is the ratio of potential gain to potential loss. Measured to our ₹303 base target, it is 6.7 to 1 from ₹211.26 against 2.7 to 1 at ₹225.97 [118]. The cost of waiting is that the stock may never come back, and we accept that.

web_blocks.intro: A support zone is the price band where a pullback should meet buyers, and a stop is the price at which we conclude the idea has failed. Greaves sits 8.6% above its 10-week average, so we do not chase it. The zone is ₹205.02–₹211.26 and the stop is ₹197.60; the table shows the entry, risk and sizing arithmetic that applies only if the pullback arrives.

web_blocks.text: The ₹197.60 stop sits 2.4% under the 30-week SMA and just 0.12% under the 200-day EMA at ₹197.84, below the 20-day SMA, the 4H 50 SMA and the pivot midpoint (our calculation [118]). A close beneath all of those is a failed Stage 2 hold. Risk per share is ₹13.66 (6.5%) from ₹211.26 and ₹7.42 (3.6%) from ₹205.02, but ₹28.37 (12.6%, about 2.9 ATRs) from today's price. Sizing uses a 50 bps risk budget on ₹42.92 lakh of net worth. The Zerodha account holds no Greaves, and cash is ₹5.75 lakh, 13.4% of net worth [118].

Greaves is not in NSE's F&O segment, so the options verdict is NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID and the view can be expressed only in cash equity [117][118]. No TradingView session was open in Chrome during the run, so every reading here rests on public data.

web_blocks.takeaway: Each level pairs a price with an event. A price break without the Q3 FY27 margin evidence does not earn an upgrade, and a margin beat without the price break does not remove supply. Cash-flow and funding triggers sit in Chapter 9.

web_blocks.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
paragraphs: The chart says the trend is up and the move is hot. It does not say who is buying, and the volume is too mixed to tell. A conditional business earns a place on the list only at a price that pays for the risk, and that price is below Friday's close.

book_paragraphs: Picture a staircase. Each flight rises, then the stair levels off into a landing, then rises again. A stock in a healthy uptrend climbs the same way, and the landings are where careful people get on. Stan Weinstein, who studied thousands of charts, gave those flights and landings names. Stage 1 is the flat floor at the bottom. Stage 2 is the climb. Stage 3 is the long landing at the top where the rise stalls. Stage 4 is the fall back down. His test is simple: is the price above its 30-week average, and is that average rising? Greaves Cotton passes it.

That is good news, and you should hold it lightly. Passing the Stage 2 test means the stock is allowed onto our list. It does not mean it should be bought today. Chapter 7 told you the business is conditional, not great, so the chart has to do something the business cannot: hand us a good price. Before going on, a word on dates, because honesty about them matters. The levels in this chapter use the Friday 13 November close of ₹225.97. Some of our supporting fields come from the Thursday bar, ₹223.18, one session older. The two sets agree on every structural point.

There is also a missing witness. A popular Stage 2 dashboard, dated 8 November, does not list Greaves among its 465 names, so there is no independent vote that the stock is a market leader. We worked out a likely reason. The share price a week earlier was about ₹203.4, barely 0.4% above its 30-week line of ₹202.50. When the dashboard was built, the stock was standing on the edge. The 11% jump of that week took it clearly over. We cannot prove that explanation, but it fits.

Look at the averages as a set of landings. The 10-week average is ₹208.14, the 50-day ₹204.14, the 30-week ₹202.50, the 200-day exponential average ₹197.84. Add the 20-day at ₹200.31 and the pivot midpoint at ₹200.30 and you have a thick shelf between about ₹198 and ₹208. The price, ₹225.97, is standing about 9% above the shelf's top. Picture a lift that has run ahead of the staircase. If it comes back to the landing, the structure is healthy. If it falls through, something has changed.

Now listen to the three clocks. A daily clock reads 66.5 on the RSI, which scales recent gains against losses from 0 to 100. The weekly clock reads 57.4, comfortable. The four-hour clock reads 71.3, stretched. When the short clock runs hot over a calmer long one, the usual resolution is a cooling-off, either a pause or a pullback, while the slower clock catches up. That is the tempo gap, and it is why the options module labels this setup extended.

Then look up. A stock that has been this high before carries memory. Holders who bought near ₹244, ₹259 and ₹272 are sitting on losses and many will sell when they get back to even. The first test is at ₹229, only 1.4% above Friday's close. Beyond it lies a band of supply running to ₹272. The honest limit of our data is that we infer this from the price record and do not have volume by price.

What about the crowd? Volume is the footprint of big buyers. On Friday the stock traded 2.87 million shares, 1.31 times its 30-day average, on a rise of 1.25%. That is the one strong day. But if you take Friday out, the nine sessions before it traded about 1.50 million shares a day, roughly two-thirds of the 30-day average, while the price rose most of its 11% for the week. The ledger also counts six down days on heavy volume in the past 25 sessions. Smart money does not hide forever, and today it is not obviously buying.

Strength against the index shows a similar split. Over 63 sessions Greaves is about 9.5% ahead. Over 28 sessions it is about 14.9% behind, because it fell from its ₹271.90 high before it bounced. The broad market is in an uptrend, but narrow: 61% of the Nifty-500 pool sits above its 50-day average, and 52% above its 200-day. The sector picture, as of the dashboard's date, is patchy too: Engineered Goods is dense with Stage 2 names, Vehicle Finance and Pumps are thin. The stock has support, not leadership.

There is a rule that protects you from your own excitement. Our no-FOMO rule says that when a stock is more than 10% above its 10-week average, you do not buy it. Greaves is 8.57% above. Inside the cap, so the gate is open. But 10% above the average is about ₹229, almost exactly the first resistance. A few rupees more and the gate shuts by itself. Our own posture is firmer than the gate: wait.

So is there a short-term momentum edge today? We say no, not for a chaser. The price is more than two ATRs above its 50-day average. ATR, the average true range, is the typical daily swing, about ₹10 for this stock. A chaser also faces supply just overhead, uneven volume and a hot four-hour clock. The edge, if there is one, belongs to the patient. If the price falls back to the ₹205 to ₹211 shelf, the stop at ₹197.60 is only 3.6% to 6.5% away, and our ₹303 base target is more than six times that risk. At today's price the same target is only 2.7 times the risk. Asymmetry, the ratio of what you can win to what you can lose, is what we are waiting for.

The stop is not arbitrary. ₹197.60 sits just under the 200-day exponential average and under the whole shelf. A close below it means the staircase has failed. And because Greaves has no listed options, you cannot buy convexity cheaply; the only instrument is the share itself. That is another reason to be careful with the entry. A lift that has run ahead of the staircase is not an invitation. Livermore's old line, that his sitting, not his thinking, made the money, applies here: the job is to sit until the price comes to you.

Which levels would change our mind? A weekly close below ₹202.50 weakens the structure. A close below ₹197.60 rejects the setup. A close above ₹271.90 on strong volume, with the third-quarter core margin at 13% or better, starts an upgrade review. Nothing in between changes the plan. The next chapter puts the business and the chart together, hears the bull and the bear, and says what to do with the money.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: A strong chart is a fact about the past. It describes where buyers have been and says little about who is still buying. When the chart and the business disagree about quality, let the price be the tiebreaker, and be willing to wait for it.

question: What is the tape saying, and is there an edge in acting now?
